newsitem.title: USA: NIMO questions NYPA power sale to Cascade.
newsitem.headline: NIMO questions NYPA power sale to Cascade.

text.p: Niagara Mohawk Power Corp (NIMO), struggling with the New York Power Authority (NYPA) for new business, said Thursday it is questioning the legality of NYPA's power contract with a major industrial customer.

NIMO argues NYPA's contract with Cascades Niagara Falls Inc, a paper recycling company, goes beyond NYPA's charter to provide electricity for economic development, increase electric demand, or to bring new customers into the state.
Instead, the agreement only serves existing load, said NIMO spokeswoman Kerry Burns.
"(NYPA's) power is supposed to be for expansion power, not power for existing load. It's displacing load Niagara Mohawk is currently serving," she said.
Burns said NIMO and Cascades reached a supply agreement in which Cascades would buy power at a cheaper rate than the one negotiated with NYPA.
The NIMO/Cascades pact still needs approval by the New York State Public Service Commission.

NYPA earlier Thursday said it has requested an order from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to stop NIMO from cutting transmission service to NYPA's upstate New York customers on the basis NIMO's action was anti-competitive.

This week NIMO said it will teminate a two-part contract with NYPA on May 24. The two-part contract calls for NIMO to buy power from NYPA's 832 MW Fitzpatrick plant at above-market price and to carry additional energy from that plant to certain industrial customers.
Burns noted the New York commission concluded that the NIMO/NYPA contract was uneconomic in 1995. NIMO exercised its right to terminate the pact after several attempts to negotiate new terms failed.
NIMO asked the state commission for permission to provide electricity at a discounted price to those customers affected by the termination of the NYPA agreement.
